Key Insights & Recommendations

  • Average daily steps are 10574, with highest segment among workout type 'Running' at 10721 steps.
  • Workout participation rate is 83.1% based on workout_type != 'None' rule; dataset contains no 'None' records, indicating universally logged workouts.
  • Steps and calories are positively correlated (r=0.973), suggesting step-driven interventions can influence calorie-burn outcomes.
  • Sleep and stress show inverse correlation (r=-0.008), and average sleep declines as stress level rises.
  • Yearly trend: steps moved from 10963 (2015) to 10271 (2025).
  • Product recommendation: Build workout-type-adaptive step goals and nudges, prioritizing lower-step segments (lowest mood and workout-type cohorts) to reduce engagement dispersion.
  • Engagement recommendation: Use monthly campaign timing around lower-participation months identified in seasonality chart; pair with challenge mechanics tied to steps and calories due to their positive coupling.
  • Wellness recommendation: Add proactive recovery prompts for high-stress/low-sleep patterns; trigger educational content when user-level stress rises and sleep declines.
